thread:
raj: Heads-up — I rolled out the new int4 bringup (q3b-reranker-int4) to dedicated yesterday. NDCG improved ~1.8% but MRR dropped ~6% vs baseline. dumping small sample diffs below, need quick triage.

ci-bot: deploy succeeded: q3b-reranker-int4 @dedicated-pool-7 (2026-03-20T22:14:25Z) :white_check_mark:

emma: ugh. 6% MRR is pretty big. any obvious candidate-order flips in the sample?

raj: pasted two short examples where top1 changed from relevant->irrelevant. looks like short queries are most affected.

sophie: can you paste the exact eval config? seqlen, tokenizer, tie-handling? small things here bite MRR.

raj: eval config snippet:
```
model: q3b-reranker-int4
dataset: prod_holdout_v2
metrics: [ndcg@10, mrr@10]
preproc:
  tokenizer: hf/tok-v3
  max_tokens: 512
  doc_trim: tail
tie_break: first
candidate_pool: top50
```

raj: sample 1 (query: "reset password")
- baseline order: [docA(rel), docB, docC]
- int4 order: [docB, docA, docC]  <-- top1 moved

raj: sample 2 (query: "install gazebo ubuntu")
- baseline: [docX(rel), docY, docZ]
- int4: [docY, docZ, docX]  <-- relevant pushed to 3

mike: did the preprocessing change? are we stripping HTML/anchors the same way? sometimes metadata tokens shift ranking for short queries.

raj: same preproc pipeline invoked. but I did flip quant backend to use fused-kernel path on dedicated GPUs. could that reorder floating ops and cause score ties to break differently?

emma: yes, quantization can shrink score gaps -> tie-break sensitivity increases. tie_break: first vs random vs score-stable matters. if many candidates are within epsilon, int4 might flip ranks.

sophie: quick experiment: recompute scores and sort by (score, -doc_length) to emulate deterministic tie break and see if MRR recovers. Also compare score histograms (delta between top1 and top2).

raj: ran quick script on sample batch. hist summarized: for int4 top1-top2 delta mean = 0.012, baseline = 0.036. so gaps are smaller.

emma: that aligns. smaller deltas -> more sensitivity. Options: 1) apply score calibration (temp scaling) 2) change tie_break to prefer longer doc or source trust 3) increase numeric precision for final scoring pass (fp16 fallback)

mike: fp16 fallback for final dot-prod is feasible but will cost latency. what's SLO?

raj: SLO is 80ms p95; int4 path keeps us ~55ms. fp16 fallback would push to ~70ms for rerank-only stage, still within SLO but reduces cost savings.

emma: can we try post-quant calibration quickly? simple linear scaling on logits per-batch to match baseline mean/var. cheap and might restore ordering.

sophie: also check tokenization differences — I saw earlier that HF tok-v3 was updated with a new normalization that strips punctuation differently. short queries could be tokenized into fewer tokens changing attention patterns.

raj: good call. I re-run tokenizer parity on 1k queries. parity rate = 99.2% but mismatches cluster in short queries (<=3 tokens).

emma: hmm 0.8% mismatch concentrated on short queries could map to the MRR drop. but MRR drop seems larger than that mismatch fraction suggests. sounds like a compound effect: tokenization + score quant noise.

mike: propose 2-step mitigation: revert to fp16 final-scorer for candidate top10 (cheap since only 10 items), and run calibration job as a follow-up. That keeps int4 cost benefits for majority of ops.

raj: implemented a variant: int4 path but convert top-k candidate embeddings to fp16 and recompute final scores. ran smoke on 1000 queries: MRR delta vs baseline = -0.8% (much better). perf p95 bumped to 62ms.

emma: that's promising. can you run A/B for 100k queries from prod_holdout and report ndcg/mrr? also include breakdown by query length bucket.

raj: scheduling now. quick note: found one more oddity — we weren't normalizing candidate embeddings before dot product in the fp16 fallback path (bug). that amplifies disparity. fixed locally for the A/B run.

sophie: great catch. normalization vs no-normalization explains directional flips. normalization reduces magnitude differences that quant amplifies.

ci-bot: perf-run queued: rerank-int4-fallback-A/B (100k queries) — started 2026-03-21T00:02:10Z

mike: if A/B confirms recovery, I'd recommend keeping int4 main path + fp16 topk fallback as rolling default and open a ticket to upstream quant backend to preserve final-score precision.

emma: agree. and add a regression test in our eval harness that asserts MRR within X% on short-query slice after quant bringups. maybe <1% degradation.

raj: will add test: tests/evals/test_quant_mrr_regression.py with sampleset short_query_holdout. also include tokenization parity check.

emma: thanks. small ask — in the A/B results pls include sample queries where top1 flipped and candidate text to help labelers if we need to inspect ground truth. those are most instructive.

raj: will attach diffs when job completes. tagging @sophie for evaluation thresholds and @mike for infra followups. :pray:
